# Craft Discipline

## Overview

10 self-discipline checkpoints for the `software-engineer`.
Run at every COMMIT & VERIFY phase, before committing.

**What this skill is NOT:** a review contract. The reviewer does not read
this skill. It audits artifacts independently through its own gates.

## Checkpoints

Execute in order. Each checkpoint must pass before proceeding.

### C1 — Acceptance test passes

```bash
dotnet test --filter "Category=Acceptance"
```

The acceptance test targeted by this iteration MUST pass. No `[Skip]`.

### C2 — All unit tests pass

```bash
dotnet test
```

Zero red tests, except the committed acceptance tests of the story's scenarios not delivered yet (`outside-in-tdd` → All Acceptance Tests First). Zero ignored tests.

### C3 — Build passes

```bash
dotnet build
```

All projects compile without warnings. Treat warnings as errors.

### C4 — Static analysis passes

Verify that the linter/analyzer reports no new findings.

### C5 — No skipped tests or placeholder assertions

No `[Skip]`, `[Ignore]`, `#if false`, disabling comments,
or placeholder assertions in test bodies
(`assert.fail()` / `Assert.Fail()` / `Assert.True(false, ...)` /
`throw new NotImplementedException()` / `throw new Error('not implemented')`).
Skipped tests and placeholder assertions are both theater —
they pass the compile gate but assert nothing.

### C6 — No mocks in Domain/Application

Check UnitTest files:
- No `A.Fake<>()`, `Mock<>()`, `Substitute.For<>()`
  on a Domain or Application type.
- Mocks allowed ONLY on output gateways (repositories, external services).

### C7 — Business language verified

Test names, variables, and assertions use business vocabulary
(see the project's FR→EN lexicon). No `test1`, `data`, `ProcessData`.

### C8 — mutation stays out of the delivery

Run no mutation tool, mutation gate or `/skraft-mutation`: the project's CI runs mutation. The
developer runs `/skraft-mutation`; when they ask to kill its survivors, load `mutation-testing`.

### C9 — Conventional commit format

Use `git commit -s` with `type(feature): subject`, e.g.
`test(loyalty-discount): cover expired membership`. For a known issue, end the
body with `Refs: #N` for intermediate work or `Closes #N` (no colon) only when the whole
issue is genuinely finished and all required gates pass. Omit the issue line
when unknown.

### C10 — Object Calisthenics on Domain

Verify the 9 rules (see [references/object-calisthenics.md](references/object-calisthenics.md)).
Applicable to Domain code only.

### C11 — Parametrize Variations

Multiple input variants for the same behavior MUST be a single parameterized test
(`[Theory]/[InlineData]` in .NET, `@ParameterizedTest` in Java, `pytest.mark.parametrize` in Python,
`it.each` / `test.each` in TypeScript and JavaScript),
not duplicated test methods. One test method per behavior, one row per case.

## When to Execute

A pre-approved, staged documentation-only change with no applicable executable tests, build, or mutation targets is not a code COMMIT & VERIFY cycle. Check the exact approved content and changed paths, run applicable whitespace checks, and apply C9; do not invent code-gate results or create code-evidence artifacts.

| TDD Phase | Applicable Checkpoints |
|-----------|------------------------|
| PREPARE | None |
| RED | None |
| SYNTHESIZE-GREEN | C3 only (build) |
| COMMIT & VERIFY | **All (C1-C11)** |

## On Failure

- Red checkpoint → fix BEFORE committing.
- No exceptions, no `--ignore`.
- After 3 attempts on the same checkpoint: revert to green + escalate.

# Clean Architecture Testing

## Overview

Defines **where** to test and **with which doubles** in a Clean Architecture solution. Language-agnostic. Does NOT redefine the TDD cycle — that is owned by `outside-in-tdd`.

**Core principle:** every test enters through **one boundary** and asserts at the next boundary. Choice of double follows the layer, not convenience.

**REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use `outside-in-tdd` for the RED → SYNTHESIZE-GREEN → COMMIT cycle. This skill only routes you to the correct layer and doubles.

## The Iron Rule for Domain Tests

**Default = Application-level acceptance test.** Do NOT write Domain tests by default.

Extract a Domain test ONLY when a business rule:
- Has complex invariants or a large edge-case matrix, AND
- Is extracted into a reusable Policy / Domain Service / Specification.

**NEVER test directly:**
- Constructors (unless they enforce complex invariants)
- Simple value objects (covered by usage in Application acceptance tests)
- Getters / setters / DTOs / ViewModels / passive data structures

A test asserting `new PolicyNumber("abc").value == "abc"` is noise. It tests the compiler, not behavior.

## Test Project Organization

**Rule: exactly two test projects per bounded context**, regardless of language.

| Test project | Targets | Contains |
|---|---|---|
| `<Context>.UnitTest` | Domain + Application | Domain unit tests (rare, extracted rules) + Application acceptance tests (mocks on output gateways, in-memory fakes) |
| `<Context>.IntegrationTest` | Infrastructure + API + Architecture | Infrastructure integration tests (real containers), API end-to-end tests (in-process app host), architecture tests |

### Per-language mapping

| Ecosystem | `UnitTest` project | `IntegrationTest` project |
|---|---|---|
| .NET | `tests/<Context>.UnitTest/` csproj | `tests/<Context>.IntegrationTest/` csproj |
| Java (Maven / Gradle) | `<context>-unit-test` module | `<context>-integration-test` module |
| Python | `tests/unit/` package | `tests/integration/` package |
| React front end (Vitest) | `tests/unit/` folder | `tests/integration/` folder |
| TypeScript / Node | `test/unit/` workspace | `test/integration/` workspace |

### Multi-context solutions

One pair per bounded context. Shared helpers (fakes, builders) live in a separate non-test project (`TestKit` / `tests-shared`) referenced by both.

### Test folder naming

Test class folders and namespaces are named after the **feature or behavior** under test — never
after the GitHub issue, story ID, or sprint.

| Wrong | Right |
|---|---|
| `EligibilityCheck/STORY-42/` | `EligibilityCheck/` |
| `tests/OrderSubmission/issue-105/` | `tests/OrderSubmission/` |
| `PlaceOrder/Sprint3/` | `PlaceOrder/` |

One folder per feature or bounded behavior. The folder name answers "what does this test?"
not "which ticket created it?"

### Forbidden combinations

| Wrong | Why |
|---|---|
| Single test project mixing unit + integration | Slow tests pollute the fast loop; developers start skipping the suite |
| Splitting by production layer (`*.Domain.Test`, `*.Application.Test`, …) | Explodes project count, fights the boundary policy |
| End-to-end app host test in `UnitTest` | API tests need full composition — belong in `IntegrationTest` |
| Real container (DB / broker) in `UnitTest` | Breaks the <1 s suite promise |
| Architecture scanner test in `UnitTest` | Architecture tests are a CI gate, not a development loop |
| Third test project outside `UnitTest` / `IntegrationTest` | Creates a blind spot outside the two-speed suite; all tests belong to one of the two defined projects |

## Testing Strategy per Layer

| Layer | Test type | Entry point | Doubles | Target speed | When to write |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SharedKernel** | None | — | — | — | Never (interfaces + base classes, no logic) |
| **Domain** | Pure unit (rare) | Policy / Domain Service / Specification | None (real objects) | <10 ms | Only for extracted complex rules |
| **Application** | Acceptance (sociable) | Command / Query handler or UseCase | Mocks on output gateways, hand-written in-memory fakes for stateful reuse | <100 ms | **Default** — one per Gherkin scenario |
| **Infrastructure** | Integration | Gateway adapter (repository, read service, message handler) | Real I/O via containers (DB, broker); external APIs via contract mock server | 1-5 s | One per adapter contract |
| **API** | End-to-end | HTTP endpoint via in-process app host | Real internal stack; contract mock server for downstream externals | 1-5 s | Walking skeleton + one happy path per endpoint |
| **Architecture** | Static analysis | Assembly / module scan | None | <1 s | One rule per constraint, CI gate |

## Doubles Policy (by role, not by library)

| Role | Use for | Never for |
|---|---|---|
| **Real domain object** | Always, at every layer that touches Domain | — |
| **Mock / stub on output gateway** | Output gateways at Application level (repository, dispatcher, external service interfaces) | Domain objects, Application handlers |
| **Hand-written in-memory fake** | Reusable across many Application tests, stateful scenarios | One-off single-test cases |
| **Real container** (DB, broker) | Infrastructure adapter tests exclusively | Application or Domain tests |
| **Contract mock server** (for external APIs / brokers) | Infrastructure adapter tests against externals; API E2E with downstream externals | Internal domain logic, Application handlers |
| **In-process app host** (boots the full API) | API layer end-to-end tests exclusively | Application, Domain, Infrastructure |
| **Architecture scanner** | Architecture tests | Any behavioral test |

Pick one mocking library per solution and stick to it. Same for the app host factory. Mixing libraries across tests is a smell.

## Per-Layer Examples (pseudo-code)

Full runnable examples: [examples-dotnet.md](references/examples-dotnet.md) (.NET), [examples-java.md](references/examples-java.md) (Java / Spring Boot, Maven), [examples-python.md](references/examples-python.md) (Python, pytest) and [examples-react.md](references/examples-react.md) (React, Vitest). The roles are identical across languages.

### Application — acceptance test

```
given repository := mock of IOrderRepository
  and dispatcher := mock of IDomainEventDispatcher
  and handler := new PlaceOrderCommandHandler(repository, dispatcher)

when handler.handle(PlaceOrderCommand(id, "Alice"))

then repository received add(order where order.customerName == "Alice") exactly once
 and dispatcher received dispatch(events containing OrderPlacedEvent) exactly once
```

### Infrastructure — integration test

```
given db := start Postgres container
  and ctx := connect(db.connectionString) and migrate
  and sut := new OrderRepository(ctx)
  and order := Order.create(id, "Alice")

when sut.add(order)

then ctx.orders contains one row with customerName == "Alice"
```

### API — end-to-end test

```
given appHost := boot in-process app host
  and client := appHost.createHttpClient()

when response := client.POST("/orders", { customerName: "Alice" })

then response.status == 201
 and response.location is not null
```

### Architecture — layer rule

```
assert each project references only its inner neighbour
  (Api → Infrastructure → Application → Domain)

assert types in Domain depend only on Domain and the language core
assert types in Application depend only on Application, Domain and the language core
  else fail with "Violations: ..."
```

The language core excludes I/O, network and persistence. Allow-list the business code: a rule that only forbids the other layers lets every framework through.

## External Contract Mocks (Infrastructure & API)

When an adapter (Infrastructure) or endpoint (API) talks to an external HTTP / gRPC / async API:

- Start a **contract mock server** from the external's published contract (OpenAPI, gRPC proto, AsyncAPI).
- Point the adapter's client at the mock's URL / topic.
- In API end-to-end tests, wire downstream externals to the mock through DI overrides.
- The same contract file can later validate real responses (contract verification).

Out of scope for this skill — see `api-contract-testing` *(upcoming)* for the full pattern.

## Decision Tree — Which Test Layer?

```dot
digraph which_layer {
    node [shape=box];
    change [shape=diamond, label="What is the change?"];
    usecase [label="Use case orchestration\n(load/save/publish)"];
    gateway [label="Gateway adapter\n(DB, HTTP, broker)"];
    http [label="HTTP endpoint wiring"];
    rule [label="Complex reusable rule\n(many edge cases)"];
    boundary [label="Layer boundary rule"];
    app_test [style=filled, label="Application acceptance test\n(mocks on output gateways)"];
    infra_test [style=filled, label="Infrastructure integration test\n(real container / contract mock)"];
    api_test [style=filled, label="API end-to-end test\n(in-process app host)"];
    domain_test [style=filled, label="Domain unit test\n(pure)"];
    arch_test [style=filled, label="Architecture test\n(static scan)"];

    change -> usecase -> app_test;
    change -> gateway -> infra_test;
    change -> http -> api_test;
    change -> rule -> domain_test;
    change -> boundary -> arch_test;
}
```

Extended tree with tie-breakers: [doubles-decision-tree.md](references/doubles-decision-tree.md).

## Anti-Patterns

| Anti-pattern | Fix |
|---|---|
| Testing `new ValueObject(x).value == x` | Delete. Covered by usage in Application test. |
| Mocking a domain object | Use the real aggregate. Mock only output gateways. |
| Real container in an Application-level test | Move to Infrastructure layer or use an in-memory fake. |
| Shared global container across test classes | One container per test class, isolated lifecycle. |
| In-process app host used to test a handler | Switch to an Application-level test with mocks. |
| No architecture test guarding layer references | Add the rule. Layer discipline must be enforced by CI, not reviews. |
| Architecture test that only forbids the other layers | Allow-list what Domain and Application may depend on; a framework or an I/O client passes a layer-only rule. |
| In-memory fake DB provider used as Infrastructure test | Infrastructure tests MUST use the real provider via real container. In-memory providers silently accept invalid SQL. |
| One acceptance test covers 5 rules | Split: one Gherkin scenario = one test. |
| Duplicating acceptance coverage with a Domain test on the same rule | Delete the Domain test unless the rule was extracted. |

## Red Flags — STOP

These thoughts signal you're about to violate the policy:

- "I'll add a quick test on this constructor for safety."
- "Let me mock this aggregate to simplify the test."
- "I need an in-memory DB provider here because real containers are slow."
- "This handler test needs a real DB to verify my query."
- "Architecture tests slow down the build — I'll skip them."
- "A Domain test per value object will bump coverage."

**All of these mean: stop and re-read the table.** Coverage is not the goal. Behavior at the correct boundary is.

## References

- [examples-dotnet.md](references/examples-dotnet.md) — full runnable .NET examples (FakeItEasy, Testcontainers, in-process app host, architecture scanner)
- [examples-java.md](references/examples-java.md) — full runnable Java / Spring Boot examples (JUnit 5, Mockito, Testcontainers, ArchUnit)
- [examples-python.md](references/examples-python.md) — runnable Python examples (pytest, hand-written fakes, testcontainers, FastAPI `TestClient`, import-linter)
- [examples-react.md](references/examples-react.md) — runnable React examples (Vitest, in-memory gateways, Testing Library, MSW, the ESLint guard)
- [architecture-rules.md](references/architecture-rules.md) — complete architecture rule set (project references + allow-list; .NET implementation)
- [doubles-decision-tree.md](references/doubles-decision-tree.md) — extended decision tree with tie-breakers

2. # Approved implementation plan — checkout pricing quote

18. layer tests.

25.

27.   `CalculateLoyaltyDiscountQuery(int SubtotalCents, LoyaltyTier LoyaltyTier, string? PromoCode = null)`,

33. - `QuoteCheckout.Handle(QuoteCheckoutQuery)` with

35.   returning `CheckoutQuote(int PayableCents, int ShippingCents, int TotalCents)` (S14).
36. - `LoyaltyTier` gains `Platinum` with S9.

39. 
40. | Scenario | Rule |
41. |---|---|

52. | S11 | Standard shipping 490 cents under 5 000 cents payable, 0 from 5 000 |
53. | S12 | Standard shipping is 0 for Gold and Platinum |
54. | S13 | Express shipping 990 cents, 0 for Platinum |
55. | S14 | Checkout total = payable total of the discount quote + shipping fee on that payable total |
56.

 # Approved implementation plan — checkout pricing quote
 
 ## Dispatch context
 
 - Story: `discount`
 - Project slug: `pricing`
 - Status: approved for DELIVER
 - Scenarios, in delivery order: S1 to S14 (`features/discount.feature`)
 
 ## Solution shape
 
 This is a .NET 10 Clean Architecture solution. Production projects live under
 `src/`: Domain has no project dependency; Application depends only on Domain;
 Infrastructure depends on Application; API composes Application and Infrastructure.
 Exactly two test projects live under `tests/`: `CheckoutPricing.UnitTest` targets
 Domain + Application and `CheckoutPricing.IntegrationTest` owns architecture and outer
 layer tests.
 
 All amounts are integer cents. Percentages round down to the cent.
 
 ## Boundaries
 
 Every scenario enters through one of these signatures; keep them exactly.
 
 - `CalculateLoyaltyDiscount.Handle(CalculateLoyaltyDiscountQuery)` with
   `CalculateLoyaltyDiscountQuery(int SubtotalCents, LoyaltyTier LoyaltyTier, string? PromoCode = null)`,
   returning `LoyaltyDiscountQuote(int SubtotalCents, int DiscountCents, int TotalCents, LoyaltyTier LoyaltyTier)`.
   The `PromoCode` parameter arrives with S4; S1 to S3 calls stay unchanged.
 - `CalculateShippingFee.Handle(CalculateShippingFeeQuery)` with
   `CalculateShippingFeeQuery(int PayableTotalCents, LoyaltyTier LoyaltyTier, bool Express = false)`,
   returning the fee in cents as `int` (S11 to S13).
 - `QuoteCheckout.Handle(QuoteCheckoutQuery)` with
   `QuoteCheckoutQuery(int SubtotalCents, LoyaltyTier LoyaltyTier, string? PromoCode, bool Express)`,
   returning `CheckoutQuote(int PayableCents, int ShippingCents, int TotalCents)` (S14).
 - `LoyaltyTier` gains `Platinum` with S9.
 
 ## Rules, by scenario
 
 | Scenario | Rule |
 |---|---|
 | S1 | Loyalty rate: Bronze 5 %, Silver 10 %, Gold 15 % |
 | S2 | The loyalty part is capped at 2 000 cents |
 | S3 | A subtotal under 3 000 cents gets no loyalty part |
 | S4 | `WELCOME5` adds 500 cents after the loyalty part |
 | S5 | Cap and minimum apply to the loyalty part only |
 | S6 | Promo codes compare case-insensitively |
 | S7 | `SUMMER10` adds 10 % of the subtotal minus the loyalty part, at most 1 500 cents |
 | S8 | Any other code is ignored |
 | S9 | Platinum rate 20 % |
 | S10 | The discount never exceeds the subtotal |
 | S11 | Standard shipping 490 cents under 5 000 cents payable, 0 from 5 000 |
 | S12 | Standard shipping is 0 for Gold and Platinum |
 | S13 | Express shipping 990 cents, 0 for Platinum |
 | S14 | Checkout total = payable total of the discount quote + shipping fee on that payable total |

## Core Principles (Non-Negotiable)
1. **Clean Architecture Strictness**: Project references point INWARD, one layer at a time: API -> Infrastructure -> Application -> Domain -> none. Any upward dependency is a fatal defect.
2. **Double-Loop TDD**: 1 Acceptance test (outside) -> Focused Unit tests (inside).
3. **4-Phase Cycle**: PREPARE -> RED -> SYNTHESIZE-GREEN, repeated until the scenario's acceptance test passes -> COMMIT once for the scenario. A red is never chained to a commit; a green is.
4. **Iron Rule of Tests**: NEVER modify a failing test to make it pass. Fix the implementation. If stuck after 3 attempts, restore the working copy to your last commit and escalate.
5. **No Test Theater**: Tests MUST fail if behavior changes. Zero mockist tests in Domain/Application.
6. **Token Economy**: Concise responses, no unsolicited docs, no unnecessary files.

## Test Design & Theater Prevention
These are owned by the skills — load them, do not inline rules here.

## Execution Workflow (Execute in Order)

### Prepared documentation-only handoff

Use this path only when the dispatch carries no `state.mjs handoff` block and the request or the handoff it names explicitly says the change is documentation-only, already prepared and staged, has no applicable executable tests/build/mutation targets, and requests no other deliverable. A SKRAFT DELIVER dispatch always takes the full workflow below. When the checkout is nested, enter the repository named by the handoff; run every repository command there, never in its parent workspace.

1. Read the handoff, run `git status --short` and `git diff --cached --name-only`, and inspect the patch. Confirm only the approved document is staged or changed, no untracked files exist, and its wording matches the approved text; stop if any check fails.
2. Run `git diff --cached --check` and `git diff --check`. If both pass, commit only the prepared change with `git commit -s` and `docs({feature-scope}): {concise subject}`. For a known issue, use final body line `Refs: #N` for intermediate work or `Closes #N` only when the handoff confirms the entire issue is complete; omit issue references when unknown.
3. Verify exactly one commit contains only the approved document, the checkout is clean, and the commit has the configured identity and matching sign-off. Report its hash, applicable checks, and issue disposition.

Do not enter PREPARE, RED, SYNTHESIZE-GREEN, or code COMMIT & VERIFY for this path. Do not create tests, change logs, quality-evidence logs, or QA reports, and do not claim code-test or mutation results. The explicit handoff scope overrides generic code-output requirements when those outputs are inapplicable.

### 1. PREPARE
- Load the DISTILL artefacts: the `.feature`, `test-plan-{story}.md`, `impl-plan-{story}.md`, and the **outer acceptance test(s) already authored by the acceptance-designer**. Take their paths from the handoff block; without a ref, search `.copilot-tracking/skraft-plans/{projectSlug}/`. The plans are settled: never re-plan the story.
- Take build and test commands from the stack-commands file in the handoff block. Load `resolving-stack-commands` only when the file is absent or one of its commands fails, then rewrite the file with the corrected commands.
- Take project conventions from the research document's `Project conventions` section when the handoff block lists it; do not re-derive them from the code.
- **The acceptance tests are written.** The acceptance-designer authored the acceptance test of every scenario and committed them RED in one `test` commit (`outside-in-tdd` → All Acceptance Tests First). Write no acceptance test and edit none, values included. When `git status --short` lists acceptance tests or stubs left uncommitted, run formatting and static checks on them and commit them alone in ONE `test(feature): …` commit before any production code. A scenario of the `.feature` without its acceptance test is a blocker for DISTILL: report it, never write it.
- Do NOT re-author the acceptance test or alter its input / expected values (Iron Rule of tests).
- Identify entry boundaries and expected outward effects from the existing acceptance tests + the impl-plan row of the active group. Use the use case boundary and production code that row names.
- Respect the test-plan row of the active scenario: every test you write uses its layer, use case boundary and double type, and a Domain unit test exists only where the test-plan plans one with an `Extraction Reason`. Deviate only when a loaded skill forbids the planned choice, and record `PLAN_DEVIATION: {row} — {planned} → {actual} — {rule}` in the execution journal.
- Then deliver the scenarios group by group, in the impl-plan's group order, until the LAST one (`outside-in-tdd` → All Acceptance Tests First, step 4); without groups in the plan, consecutive scenarios through the same use case that pin one rule or its edge cases form one group, with ONE green commit naming them (`feat(feature): <rule> S4–S7`); a scenario on its own is a group of one. First run the group's tests filtered to it: a scenario that already passes is covered by an earlier one — confirm with the deletion test, write no code for it, and name the covering scenario on its change-log line. The red acceptance tests left after a green commit are the scenarios still owed, never a blocker and never a reason to hand over. This dispatch ends only when every acceptance test passes and the whole suite is green, or on a blocker you report. Never park a pending scenario with `Skip` / `[Ignore]`: it stays an active, failing test.

### 2. RED (inner loop)
- The OUTER acceptance test is your first red. When it states the rule with its examples, go from its red to the code and write no unit test of your own. Otherwise write the failing test of the next rule it does not pin down: one test, or one parametrized test whose rows triangulate that rule (`craft-discipline` C11), never rows of two rules.
- **Gate**: The test must fail on a BUSINESS ASSERTION, not a compilation or setup error. (Stub just enough to compile). Never weaken or edit the acceptance test to make it pass.
- Run only the new test, filtered to it, at its quietest verbosity (`outside-in-tdd` → Run one test, then its project), and read why it fails before writing a line of production code. Commit nothing: the unit test goes into the scenario's green commit.
- **The story's `test` commit is the RED of every scenario in it.** Commit it before any production code; capture no RED run. The reviewer's `test-integrity` lens checks it after the fact. Run every inner cycle and every scenario inside this one dispatch; never stop after RED to wait for an inspection.
- **Edge cases not expressible in Gherkin** (defensive branch, exhaustive-enum fallback, combinatorial sweep of an already-decided rule — e.g. a `PolicyService`) are authored HERE via TDD, but ONLY when `test-design-mandates` Mandate 4 Gate (a) or (b) opens, and ONLY with values traceable to a decided AC. A Domain unit test the test-plan does not plan is a `PLAN_DEVIATION`. The domain class emerges from this RED — create nothing before the compile failure (`outside-in-tdd` Step 2). If the case is an UNDECIDED business decision, STOP and escalate to DISCUSS — never invent a verdict or value.

### 3. SYNTHESIZE-GREEN
- Write the production code the test demands, clean the first time. When the acceptance criterion states the rule (a rate table, a threshold, a cap, a formula), write it whole; take a smaller step only when the rule is not clear from the test.
- Write it to **Object Calisthenics** (all 9 rules, `craft-discipline` C10 → [references/object-calisthenics.md](../../skills/craft-discipline/references/object-calisthenics.md)); verify the 9 rules once per scenario, on every class of its diff, before its green commit.
- **Gate**: the test filtered to it, then its test project or module, pass. The chained green commit runs every test but the pending scenarios' acceptance tests. Do NOT refactor during Green.
- **Wiring, after every inner green.** Run `git diff --name-only`. Every production file the behavior required MUST appear. If only test files changed while the test flipped RED → GREEN, that is **Fixture Theater**: go back and write the production code.
- **Once per scenario, before its green commit:** the deletion test (revert the production change mentally; if the tests still pass, they exercise fixture state, not behavior) and the placement check (`outside-in-tdd` → Post-GREEN Wiring Verification).
- Back to RED until the scenario's acceptance test passes.

### 4. COMMIT & VERIFY (once per group of scenarios)
- Commit nothing inside a group before its green: its unit tests, its code and every format or lint fix go in one green commit. No `test`, `refactor` or `style` commit inside a group.
- Before the green, run static checks and formatting and fix every failure, never changing a line of an acceptance test.
- **Green, once, chained**: run every test except the acceptance tests of scenarios not delivered yet (`outside-in-tdd` → Run one test, then its project → Pending excluded; the last group runs the whole suite) and commit in one command that commits only when the run passes, naming each file you changed (never `.`, `-A` or a folder): `<test command> && git add <each file you changed> && git commit -s -m "feat(feature): subject" -m "Refs: #N"` in sh and PowerShell 7; in Windows PowerShell 5.1, `<test command>; if ($?) { git add <each file you changed>; if ($?) { git commit -s -m "feat(feature): subject" -m "Refs: #N" } }`. The run fails → nothing is committed: fix, run the line again.
- Use `git commit -s` with `type(feature): subject`, e.g. `feat(loyalty-discount): apply member pricing`. For a known issue, end the body with `Refs: #N` for intermediate work or `Closes #N` (no colon) only when the whole issue is genuinely finished and all required gates pass. Omit the issue line when unknown.
- **Architecture, coverage and mutation never run in the story**: you run no coverage command, no separate architecture gate, no mutation tool, mutation gate or `/skraft-mutation`, at any point of the story, and write no mutation command, config or result. The project's CI runs coverage and mutation; the developer runs `/skraft-mutation`. Never record an architecture, coverage or mutation entry in the evidence log. Tell the developer in the handover.
- Write `.copilot-tracking/skraft-plans/{projectSlug}/changes/{date}/change-log.md` once, after the evidence log, one line per commit since the DELIVER base, taken from `git log`, in the same turn as the outcome JSON (create the dated subfolder if needed; markdown file starts with `<!-- markdownlint-disable-file -->`).
- **Record the quality-gates evidence log, once, after the story's last work commit.** Load `quality-gates-evidence-contract` (schema v7, recorded gates `test.acceptance`, `test.unit`, `build.compile`, `build.lint`, `test.no-mocks-core`, `evidence.screenshots`; `commit.convention` and `test.integrity` are derived from Git by `qg-verify`) and the adapter of every stack the repository holds (`quality-gates-dotnet`, `quality-gates-javascript`, `quality-gates-python`, `quality-gates-typescript`). The evidence directory holds the log and the screenshots, nothing else, and nothing under it is ever committed. Never write or edit the log yourself: every status comes from the adapter's scripts.
  - In a .NET solution, run the adapter's `qg-collect.mjs --root . --log {evidence dir}/qg-{story}.json` once — it runs every gate, records each verdict and runs `qg-verify` — with one `--screenshot` per screenshot of a frontend story.
  - Elsewhere, run each gate through the adapter's `capture.mjs --log {that log} --gate <id>` or its no-mocks script, record screenshots or a `not_applicable` gate with its `gate-log.mjs`, then run `node "$SKRAFT_PLUGIN_ROOT/src/cli/qg-verify.mjs" --log {that log}`.

  - Hand over only on `"verdict": "pass"`, or report the failing gate. A missing or malformed log is `inconclusive` (NEEDS_REWORK), so a hidden failure fails harder than a disclosed one.

## Rework mode (handoff mode `rework`)

When the handoff block's mode line reads `rework`, the previous review's findings are the whole scope of this pass:

1. Read the previous review the block names. Skip PREPARE's planning: the plans, the acceptance tests and your previous commits stand.
2. Fix each finding with the smallest change. A production change still goes RED → SYNTHESIZE-GREEN → COMMIT through a test. A finding that only asks for a stronger test is one `test` commit that adds assertions and removes or rewrites no line; a stricter assertion that must replace one carries `PLAN_DEVIATION: <old assertion> → <new assertion>` in its body (`outside-in-tdd` → commits by pass).
3. Re-run only the gates your change invalidates:
   - production or test code changed → every gate again (`qg-collect` on .NET): a verdict recorded on another tree is stale;
   - only commit messages or the change log changed → `gate-log.mjs --log {that log} --restamp` moves the log to the new `HEAD` (it refuses when the code changed), then re-run `qg-verify`; never re-run tests;
   - the dispatch carries `Environment re-gate` → change no code; re-run only the gates the previous review names inconclusive, then re-run `qg-verify`.
4. Keep every recorded verdict your change does not invalidate.

+        AssertQuote(subtotal, tier, null, discount, total);
+
+    [Theory]
+    [InlineData(2_999, 0, 2_999)]
+    [InlineData(3_000, 450, 2_550)]
+    public void S3_NoLoyaltyDiscountUnderThirtyEuros(int subtotal, int discount, int total) =>

+

+
+    [Theory]

+    [InlineData(30_000, LoyaltyTier.Silver, 2_500, 27_500)]

+        AssertQuote(subtotal, tier, "WELCOME5", discount, total);
+
+    [Theory]
+    [InlineData("welcome5")]
+    [InlineData("Welcome5")]
+    public void S6_PromoCodesIgnoreCase(string code)
+    {
+        var quote = new CalculateLoyaltyDiscount().Handle(new CalculateLoyaltyDiscountQuery(10_000, LoyaltyTier.Silver, code));
+
+        Assert.Equal(1_500, quote.DiscountCents);
+    }
+
+    [Theory]
+    [InlineData(10_000, LoyaltyTier.Silver, 1_900, 8_100)]
+    [InlineData(30_000, LoyaltyTier.Bronze, 3_000, 27_000)]

+        AssertQuote(subtotal, tier, "SUMMER10", discount, total);

+}

# Quality Gates — .NET Adapter

Concrete recipes that bind the gates of `quality-gates-evidence-contract` to the
.NET toolchain. Loaded ONLY when the producer detects a .NET stack.

## Detection

Activate this adapter when ANY of the following resolves at the repo root:
- `*.sln` or `*.slnx`
- `Directory.Packages.props`
- `**/*.csproj`

If multiple stacks coexist, run each adapter and concatenate gate entries.

## Output paths (relative to repo root)

```
.copilot-tracking/skraft-plans/{projectSlug}/evidence/{date}/{story}/
```

Throughout this file, `$EV` is shorthand for that directory — one per story, never shared,
ignored by Git (`.copilot-tracking/skraft-plans/*/evidence/` in `.gitignore`), never committed —
and `$LOG` for `$EV/qg-{story}.json`. `<skill>` is this skill's folder, the one holding this
SKILL.md: every script below ships in `<skill>/scripts/`, never in the consumer repository.

`$EV` holds the log and the screenshots, nothing else. `capture.mjs` runs a command without a
shell, prints the last 40 lines of its output and records the gate(s) it attests in `$LOG` —
`pass` on exit 0, `fail` otherwise, the last output line as `summary`; it exits with the
command's code, in bash and PowerShell alike. No `.stdout`, `.exit` or hash file is written,
and no agent ever types a status.

## Producer flow at the end of the story

One command runs every gate, records each verdict in `$LOG` and runs `qg-verify`; it exits with
`qg-verify`'s verdict and commits nothing:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/qg-collect.mjs" --root . --log "$LOG" [--screenshot {png} …]
```

It refuses a `$LOG` Git does not ignore. It prints one line per gate, then the verdict. A `fail`
or `inconclusive` is yours to fix: fix the code, then run it again. `qg-verify` takes the DELIVER
and DISTILL bases the pipeline recorded; pass `--base` / `--red-base` only outside a pipeline.

## test.acceptance / test.unit — Tests pass

One run of the full suite attests both gates. The full suite includes the
`*.ArchitectureTests` project (NetArchTest / ArchUnitNET) when the repository has one: a broken
architecture rule fails `test.unit`. `qg-collect` writes the TRX report to a throw-away folder
outside the repository and records its counters as `metrics`. By hand:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/capture.mjs" --log "$LOG" --gate test.acceptance,test.unit -- dotnet test --nologo
```

## build.compile / build.lint — Build and static analysis

Use the analyzers wired into the build (Roslyn analyzers, `TreatWarningsAsErrors=true`): one
build attests both gates.

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/capture.mjs" --log "$LOG" --gate build.compile,build.lint -- dotnet build --nologo --no-incremental
```

## test.no-mocks-core — No mocks in Domain/Application

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/no-mocks-in-core.mjs" --root . --log "$LOG"
```

The script scans every `*.Domain` and `*.Application` project at any depth, plus the
`*.Domain.*Tests`, `*.Application.*Tests` and `*.UnitTests` projects, for mocking
frameworks (Moq, NSubstitute, FakeItEasy, AutoMoq). It prints one hit per line and records the
gate: `pass` on exit 0, `fail` with the number of hits otherwise.

## commit.convention and test.integrity — derived by qg-verify

Nothing to record: `qg-verify` reads every commit since the DELIVER base and checks its full
message, and guards every test file DISTILL's `test` commit holds — a later commit may only add
lines to it, unless its message records `PLAN_DEVIATION:`. No commit list, no cycle, no snapshot.

## evidence.screenshots — Frontend stories

A story whose commits touch a `@visual` scenario, `tests/e2e/`, a `package.json` declaring
`react` or a `playwright.config.*` records at least one screenshot taken by
`playwright-evidence`. Pass each PNG with `--screenshot`; `qg-collect` copies it into
`$EV/screenshots/` and records its sha256 (by hand: `node "<skill>/scripts/gate-log.mjs" --log "$LOG" --screenshot {png}`).

## Not run by this adapter

Architecture (`arch.boundaries`), coverage (`ci.coverage`) and mutation (`ci.mutation`) are not
pipeline gates. Coverage at 100% of Domain and Application and the mutation step run in the
project's CI; the developer runs `/skraft-mutation` by hand. Never record them in the log.

If a tool is unavailable in the environment (no SDK), the
gate is recorded `fail` with its error as summary — NOT `not_applicable`. The
contract treats unverifiable gates strictly so the lens can collapse them to
`inconclusive` upstream.

# Quality Gates Evidence Contract

A tech-agnostic schema that attests quality gates with **verdicts written by scripts and facts
read from Git**, never with prose.

## Why this exists

Truth #6 (HARNESSES BRIDGE): the LLM cannot prove a test passed by saying so.
So no agent ever writes a gate status: the stack adapter's scripts run each command and record
its exit code in the log, and `qg-verify`
(`node "<skill>/scripts/qg-verify/cli/qg-verify.mjs" --log <path>`, bundled in this skill;
`<skill>` is the folder holding this SKILL.md) derives everything else from Git — the commits
since the DELIVER base and every RED acceptance test — and judges the verdict. Nobody re-runs a
gate; the project's CI runs them again on the pull request.

## Where the artifacts live — never in Git

One directory per story, never shared with another story, **ignored by Git**. It holds the log
and, for a frontend story, its screenshots — nothing else:

```
.copilot-tracking/skraft-plans/{projectSlug}/evidence/{date}/{story}/
├── qg-{story}.json      # the evidence log (this contract): verdicts only
└── screenshots/         # evidence.screenshots, frontend stories
```

The consumer project's `.gitignore` holds this line:

```gitignore
.copilot-tracking/skraft-plans/*/evidence/
```

Nothing under `evidence/` is ever committed: not the log, not a screenshot. No tool output,
exit-code or hash file is written either. `qg-verify` fails a v7 log whose evidence directory
holds a file Git tracks.

A screenshot `ref` is relative to the project's tracking directory
(`evidence/{date}/{story}/screenshots/home.png`). Tool run folders (Stryker HTML, TRX, logs)
never land here.

The test plan (`details/{date}/test-plan-{story}.md`, written by DISTILL) stays where it is: with
the screenshots, it is what the QA reads.

## Schema (`qg-{story}.json`)

The stack adapter's scripts write it — `capture.mjs` and the no-mocks scan for each gate,
`gate-log.mjs` for screenshots and `not_applicable` gates, or `qg-collect.mjs` for all of them on
.NET. Each write stamps `repo_root_rev` with `HEAD` and `produced_at` with the time.

```json
{
  "$schema": "quality-gates-evidence/v7",
  "story": "string — story identifier, from the file name qg-{story}.json",
  "produced_at": "ISO-8601 UTC timestamp",
  "producer": "software-engineer",
  "tech_adapter": "string — the quality-gates-<tech> skill whose scripts wrote it",
  "repo_root_rev": "string — git rev-parse HEAD (the last work commit)",
  "gates": [
    {
      "id": "test.acceptance",
      "label": "Acceptance test(s) pass",
      "status": "pass | fail | not_applicable",
      "command_executed": "the command the script ran",
      "summary": "last line of its output, e.g. Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: 15",
      "metrics": { "tests_total": 15, "tests_passed": 15, "tests_failed": 0 }
    },
    {
      "id": "evidence.screenshots",
      "label": "Frontend screenshots captured",
      "status": "pass",
      "screenshots": [
        { "ref": "evidence/{date}/{story}/screenshots/home-rejected.png", "sha256": "hex sha256 of the PNG bytes" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`metrics` is optional (the .NET adapter reads it from the TRX report). A `not_applicable` gate
carries a `rationale` instead of a command.

## Gates (fixed identifiers, `type.description`)

The `id` field uses a fixed taxonomy. Tech adapters MAP their tools to these ids;
they do NOT invent new ones. Adding a gate id is a contract change (new schema version).

| id | label | what it attests | before v7 |
|----|-------|-----------------|-----------|
| `test.acceptance` | Acceptance test(s) pass | the BDD/acceptance scenario for the active story is green | G1 |
| `test.unit` | All unit tests pass | the full unit suite is green; on .NET it includes the architecture tests | G2 |
| `build.compile` | Build passes | compilation / static type-check succeeded | G3 |
| `build.lint` | Static analysis pass | linter / analyzer reported no blocking issue; carries the boundary rules of the stack (ESLint `boundaries/*`, Python `import-linter`) | G4 |
| `test.no-mocks-core` | No mocks in Domain/Application core | the adapter's scan of the Domain/Application projects and their unit tests found nothing | G7 |
| `evidence.screenshots` | Frontend screenshots captured | the story's frontend outcome is shown by at least one hashed screenshot; required for a frontend story | — |
| `commit.convention` | Conventional commit policy | *derived by `qg-verify`, never in the log*: every commit since the DELIVER base satisfies the shared policy below | G8 |
| `test.integrity` | No test tampering (RED→GREEN integrity) | *derived by `qg-verify`, never in the log*: every test file a `test` commit holds only grows afterwards | G9 |

Architecture, coverage and mutation are not pipeline gates. The project's CI runs them
(coverage with a minimal bar and no exclusion, mutation as its own step); the developer runs
`/skraft-mutation` by hand. A v7 log never carries `arch.boundaries`, `ci.coverage`,
`ci.mutation` nor any `G<N>` id: `qg-verify` reports an unknown id as `inconclusive`, and a
derived id (`commit.convention`, `test.integrity`) recorded in the log as `inconclusive` too.

The RED is DISTILL's `test` commit: every acceptance test, committed before DELIVER starts and
before the code that makes it pass. No RED run is captured, no snapshot is written, and the
producer lists no commit and no cycle: `qg-verify` reads them from Git.

A gate that is genuinely irrelevant for the story uses `status: "not_applicable"` and
MUST include a `rationale` field explaining why. `not_applicable` is **never** a substitute
for `fail` or for missing evidence.

## Frontend stories — screenshots are mandatory

A story is frontend when a commit since the DELIVER base touches at least one of:

- a `.feature` file holding a `@visual` scenario;
- a path under `tests/e2e/`;
- a `package.json` declaring `react` (dependencies, devDependencies or peerDependencies);
- a `playwright.config.*` file.

A frontend story records `evidence.screenshots` with `status: "pass"` and at least one
screenshot — `node "<adapter>/scripts/gate-log.mjs" --log "$EV/qg-{story}.json" --screenshot <png>`
copies each PNG into `evidence/{date}/{story}/screenshots/` and records its `ref` and the sha256
of its bytes. Any other story omits the gate or records it `not_applicable` with a rationale.

## Falsification surface (what qg-verify checks)

`qg-verify` takes the DELIVER base (`--base`, default: the one the pipeline recorded) and the
DISTILL base (`--red-base`, default: idem). The quality-gates lens reports its verdict and checks
only the commit policy it cannot (approved feature scope, `Refs`/`Closes` issue line).

| What | How it is falsified |
|------|---------------------|
| `repo_root_rev` | resolves, and is `HEAD` |
| evidence directory | no file under it is tracked by Git |
| `gates[].status` | written by a script from an exit code; `fail` fails the log |
| `gates[].metrics.tests_failed` | for `status: "pass"` MUST be `0` |
| `gates[].screenshots[]` | each file MUST exist; the sha256 of its bytes MUST equal the declared value |
| `commit.convention` | every commit of `base..repo_root_rev`, read from Git |
| `test.integrity` | the test files of the `test` commits since the DISTILL base are guarded: each later commit that touches one may only ADD lines (`git show` of its parent against `git show` of the commit), unless its message records `PLAN_DEVIATION:` |
| frontend detection | computed from the files of `base..repo_root_rev` at `repo_root_rev` |

A test file is a `.feature`, a file under a `test`, `tests`, `__tests__`, `spec`, `specs` or `e2e`
folder, or a file named as a test (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, `*Tests.cs`, `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`).
The production stubs DISTILL commits with the RED are not guarded: the GREEN rewrites them.

## commit.convention — Full-message verification

Each commit's actual Git message: `type(feature): subject`, with the
approved feature scope and `Signed-off-by` trailer from `git commit -s`. For a
known issue, the final body line is `Refs: #N` for intermediate work or
`Closes #N` only when the whole issue is genuinely finished and all required
gates pass. Omit the issue line when unknown.

`qg-verify` checks the syntax and the sign-off; the lens checks the feature scope and the issue
line from the full messages. A verified violation is `fail`; a message nobody can read is
`inconclusive`.

## Producer rules (software-engineer side)

- Record the gates **once**, at the end of the story, after every work commit landed; each
  script stamps `repo_root_rev` with that last work commit, `HEAD`. Nothing is committed after it.
- The scripts refuse a log path Git does not ignore; append
  `.copilot-tracking/skraft-plans/*/evidence/` to the project's `.gitignore` in a work commit.
- Never write or edit the JSON by hand: every status comes from a script.
- Run `qg-verify` on the log before handing over; a `fail` or `inconclusive` is yours to fix.
- A failing gate is recorded `fail` and the log is still written. Do NOT delete the log to hide a
  failure — a missing log is `inconclusive` (NEEDS_REWORK), so hiding fails harder than disclosing.

## Verifier rules (qg-verify)

- `qg-verify` exits `0` pass, `1` fail, `2` inconclusive; the producer runs it on its own log
  before handing over, the reviewer runs it again, the lens reports its result.
- Any of the following → `verdict: inconclusive` (never `pass`):
  - the JSON is missing, or a required field is absent or malformed
  - a gate id is not a v7 gate (`GATE_UNKNOWN`), or a derived gate is recorded (`GATE_DERIVED`)
  - a screenshot does not exist, or its `sha256` does not match its bytes
  - `repo_root_rev` is not `HEAD` (the log describes an older tree)
  - no DELIVER base (`BASE_UNKNOWN`) or no DISTILL base (`RED_BASE_UNKNOWN`) is known
  - no `test` commit since the DISTILL base holds a test, while `test.acceptance` applies
  - a commit cannot be read
- Any of the following → `verdict: fail`:
  - a gate has `status: "fail"`
  - `metrics.tests_failed > 0` while `status: "pass"` (internal contradiction)
  - a commit since the DELIVER base violates the shared `commit.convention` policy
  - a guarded test file lost or changed a line without a `PLAN_DEVIATION:` in the commit
    (a `PLAN_DEVIATION` is reported as a `notice` for the lens to judge)
  - a file of the evidence directory is tracked by Git (`EVIDENCE_COMMITTED`)
  - a frontend story records no screenshot (`SCREENSHOTS_MISSING`)

## Schema versioning

`$schema: "quality-gates-evidence/v7"` is part of the contract. Bump the version
when adding/removing gates or fields; old logs MUST still be parseable with their
declared version.

- **v7** — gate ids become `type.description` (`test.acceptance`, `test.unit`, `build.compile`,
  `build.lint`, `test.no-mocks-core`; `commit.convention` and `test.integrity` derived from Git).
  Removes `G5` (architecture: covered by `test.unit` on .NET and `build.lint` on TypeScript and
  Python), `G6` (mutation: the project's CI, `/skraft-mutation` by hand) and `G11` (coverage: the
  project's CI). The log holds verdicts only: no `stdout_ref`, `stdout_sha256`, `stdout_tail`,
  `exit_code_ref`, `commits_covered` nor `test_integrity` — scripts write each status, and
  `qg-verify` reads the commits and the RED tests from Git. Adds `evidence.screenshots`, required
  for a frontend story. The log and the screenshots live in a Git-ignored directory;

data.content:
# Quality Gates Evidence Contract

A tech-agnostic schema that attests quality gates with **verdicts written by scripts and facts
read from Git**, never with prose.

## Why this exists

Truth #6 (HARNESSES BRIDGE): the LLM cannot prove a test passed by saying so.
So no agent ever writes a gate status: the stack adapter's scripts run each command and record
its exit code in the log, and `qg-verify`
(`node "<skill>/scripts/qg-verify/cli/qg-verify.mjs" --log <path>`, bundled in this skill;
`<skill>` is the folder holding this SKILL.md) derives everything else from Git — the commits
since the DELIVER base and every RED acceptance test — and judges the verdict. Nobody re-runs a
gate; the project's CI runs them again on the pull request.

## Where the artifacts live — never in Git

One directory per story, never shared with another story, **ignored by Git**. It holds the log
and, for a frontend story, its screenshots — nothing else:

```
.copilot-tracking/skraft-plans/{projectSlug}/evidence/{date}/{story}/
├── qg-{story}.json      # the evidence log (this contract): verdicts only
└── screenshots/         # evidence.screenshots, frontend stories
```

The consumer project's `.gitignore` holds this line:

```gitignore
.copilot-tracking/skraft-plans/*/evidence/
```

Nothing under `evidence/` is ever committed: not the log, not a screenshot. No tool output,
exit-code or hash file is written either. `qg-verify` fails a v7 log whose evidence directory
holds a file Git tracks.

A screenshot `ref` is relative to the project's tracking directory
(`evidence/{date}/{story}/screenshots/home.png`). Tool run folders (Stryker HTML, TRX, logs)
never land here.

The test plan (`details/{date}/test-plan-{story}.md`, written by DISTILL) stays where it is: with
the screenshots, it is what the QA reads.

## Schema (`qg-{story}.json`)

The stack adapter's scripts write it — `capture.mjs` and the no-mocks scan for each gate,
`gate-log.mjs` for screenshots and `not_applicable` gates, or `qg-collect.mjs` for all of them on
.NET. Each write stamps `repo_root_rev` with `HEAD` and `produced_at` with the time.

```json
{
  "$schema": "quality-gates-evidence/v7",
  "story": "string — story identifier, from the file name qg-{story}.json",
  "produced_at": "ISO-8601 UTC timestamp",
  "producer": "software-engineer",
  "tech_adapter": "string — the quality-gates-<tech> skill whose scripts wrote it",
  "repo_root_rev": "string — git rev-parse HEAD (the last work commit)",
  "gates": [
    {
      "id": "test.acceptance",
      "label": "Acceptance test(s) pass",
      "status": "pass | fail | not_applicable",
      "command_executed": "the command the script ran",
      "summary": "last line of its output, e.g. Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: 15",
      "metrics": { "tests_total": 15, "tests_passed": 15, "tests_failed": 0 }
    },
    {
      "id": "evidence.screenshots",
      "label": "Frontend screenshots captured",
      "status": "pass",
      "screenshots": [
        { "ref": "evidence/{date}/{story}/screenshots/home-rejected.png", "sha256": "hex sha256 of the PNG bytes" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`metrics` is optional (the .NET adapter reads it from the TRX report). A `not_applicable` gate
carries a `rationale` instead of a command.

## Gates (fixed identifiers, `type.description`)

The `id` field uses a fixed taxonomy. Tech adapters MAP their tools to these ids;
they do NOT invent new ones. Adding a gate id is a contract change (new schema version).

| id | label | what it attests | before v7 |
|----|-------|-----------------|-----------|
| `test.acceptance` | Acceptance test(s) pass | the BDD/acceptance scenario for the active story is green | G1 |
| `test.unit` | All unit tests pass | the full unit suite is green; on .NET it includes the architecture tests | G2 |
| `build.compile` | Build passes | compilation / static type-check succeeded | G3 |
| `build.lint` | Static analysis pass | linter / analyzer reported no blocking issue; carries the boundary rules of the stack (ESLint `boundaries/*`, Python `import-linter`) | G4 |
| `test.no-mocks-core` | No mocks in Domain/Application core | the adapter's scan of the Domain/Application projects and their unit tests found nothing | G7 |
| `evidence.screenshots` | Frontend screenshots captured | the story's frontend outcome is shown by at least one hashed screenshot; required for a frontend story | — |
| `commit.convention` | Conventional commit policy | *derived by `qg-verify`, never in the log*: every commit since the DELIVER base satisfies the shared policy below | G8 |
| `test.integrity` | No test tampering (RED→GREEN integrity) | *derived by `qg-verify`, never in the log*: every test file a `test` commit holds only grows afterwards | G9 |

Architecture, coverage and mutation are not pipeline gates. The project's CI runs them
(coverage with a minimal bar and no exclusion, mutation as its own step); the developer runs
`/skraft-mutation` by hand. A v7 log never carries `arch.boundaries`, `ci.coverage`,
`ci.mutation` nor any `G<N>` id: `qg-verify` reports an unknown id as `inconclusive`, and a
derived id (`commit.convention`, `test.integrity`) recorded in the log as `inconclusive` too.

The RED is DISTILL's `test` commit: every acceptance test, committed before DELIVER starts and
before the code that makes it pass. No RED run is captured, no snapshot is written, and the
producer lists no commit and no cycle: `qg-verify` reads them from Git.

A gate that is genuinely irrelevant for the story uses `status: "not_applicable"` and
MUST include a `rationale` field explaining why. `not_applicable` is **never** a substitute
for `fail` or for missing evidence.

## Frontend stories — screenshots are mandatory

A story is frontend when a commit since the DELIVER base touches at least one of:

- a `.feature` file holding a `@visual` scenario;
- a path under `tests/e2e/`;
- a `package.json` declaring `react` (dependencies, devDependencies or peerDependencies);
- a `playwright.config.*` file.

A frontend story records `evidence.screenshots` with `status: "pass"` and at least one
screenshot — `node "<adapter>/scripts/gate-log.mjs" --log "$EV/qg-{story}.json" --screenshot <png>`
copies each PNG into `evidence/{date}/{story}/screenshots/` and records its `ref` and the sha256
of its bytes. Any other story omits the gate or records it `not_applicable` with a rationale.

## Falsification surface (what qg-verify checks)

`qg-verify` takes the DELIVER base (`--base`, default: the one the pipeline recorded) and the
DISTILL base (`--red-base`, default: idem). The quality-gates lens reports its verdict and checks
only the commit policy it cannot (approved feature scope, `Refs`/`Closes` issue line).

| What | How it is falsified |
|------|---------------------|
| `repo_root_rev` | resolves, and is `HEAD` |
| evidence directory | no file under it is tracked by Git |
| `gates[].status` | written by a script from an exit code; `fail` fails the log |
| `gates[].metrics.tests_failed` | for `status: "pass"` MUST be `0` |
| `gates[].screenshots[]` | each file MUST exist; the sha256 of its bytes MUST equal the declared value |
| `commit.convention` | every commit of `base..repo_root_rev`, read from Git |
| `test.integrity` | the test files of the `test` commits since the DISTILL base are guarded: each later commit that touches one may only ADD lines (`git show` of its parent against `git show` of the commit), unless its message records `PLAN_DEVIATION:` |
| frontend detection | computed from the files of `base..repo_root_rev` at `repo_root_rev` |

A test file is a `.feature`, a file under a `test`, `tests`, `__tests__`, `spec`, `specs` or `e2e`
folder, or a file named as a test (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, `*Tests.cs`, `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`).
The production stubs DISTILL commits with the RED are not guarded: the GREEN rewrites them.

## commit.convention — Full-message verification

Each commit's actual Git message: `type(feature): subject`, with the
approved feature scope and `Signed-off-by` trailer from `git commit -s`. For a
known issue, the final body line is `Refs: #N` for intermediate work or
`Closes #N` only when the whole issue is genuinely finished and all required
gates pass. Omit the issue line when unknown.

`qg-verify` checks the syntax and the sign-off; the lens checks the feature scope and the issue
line from the full messages. A verified violation is `fail`; a message nobody can read is
`inconclusive`.

## Producer rules (software-engineer side)

- Record the gates **once**, at the end of the story, after every work commit landed; each
  script stamps `repo_root_rev` with that last work commit, `HEAD`. Nothing is committed after it.
- The scripts refuse a log path Git does not ignore; append
  `.copilot-tracking/skraft-plans/*/evidence/` to the project's `.gitignore` in a work commit.
- Never write or edit the JSON by hand: every status comes from a script.
- Run `qg-verify` on the log before handing over; a `fail` or `inconclusive` is yours to fix.
- A failing gate is recorded `fail` and the log is still written. Do NOT delete the log to hide a
  failure — a missing log is `inconclusive` (NEEDS_REWORK), so hiding fails harder than disclosing.

## Verifier rules (qg-verify)

- `qg-verify` exits `0` pass, `1` fail, `2` inconclusive; the producer runs it on its own log
  before handing over, the reviewer runs it again, the lens reports its result.
- Any of the following → `verdict: inconclusive` (never `pass`):
  - the JSON is missing, or a required field is absent or malformed
  - a gate id is not a v7 gate (`GATE_UNKNOWN`), or a derived gate is recorded (`GATE_DERIVED`)
  - a screenshot does not exist, or its `sha256` does not match its bytes
  - `repo_root_rev` is not `HEAD` (the log describes an older tree)
  - no DELIVER base (`BASE_UNKNOWN`) or no DISTILL base (`RED_BASE_UNKNOWN`) is known
  - no `test` commit since the DISTILL base holds a test, while `test.acceptance` applies
  - a commit cannot be read
- Any of the following → `verdict: fail`:
  - a gate has `status: "fail"`
  - `metrics.tests_failed > 0` while `status: "pass"` (internal contradiction)
  - a commit since the DELIVER base violates the shared `commit.convention` policy
  - a guarded test file lost or changed a line without a `PLAN_DEVIATION:` in the commit
    (a `PLAN_DEVIATION` is reported as a `notice` for the lens to judge)
  - a file of the evidence directory is tracked by Git (`EVIDENCE_COMMITTED`)
  - a frontend story records no screenshot (`SCREENSHOTS_MISSING`)

## Schema versioning

`$schema: "quality-gates-evidence/v7"` is part of the contract. Bump the version
when adding/removing gates or fields; old logs MUST still be parseable with their
declared version.

- **v7** — gate ids become `type.description` (`test.acceptance`, `test.unit`, `build.compile`,
  `build.lint`, `test.no-mocks-core`; `commit.convention` and `test.integrity` derived from Git).
  Removes `G5` (architecture: covered by `test.unit` on .NET and `build.lint` on TypeScript and
  Python), `G6` (mutation: the project's CI, `/skraft-mutation` by hand) and `G11` (coverage: the
  project's CI). The log holds verdicts only: no `stdout_ref`, `stdout_sha256`, `stdout_tail`,
  `exit_code_ref`, `commits_covered` nor `test_integrity` — scripts write each status, and
  `qg-verify` reads the commits and the RED tests from Git. Adds `evidence.screenshots`, required
  for a frontend story. The log and the screenshots live in a Git-ignored directory;
  `repo_root_rev` is `HEAD`. v1–v6 logs still verify with their `G<N>` ids, captures, snapshots
  and evidence-only commit.
- **v6** — removes gate `G10` and the per-cycle fields `red_stdout_ref`, `red_stdout_sha256`,
  `red_exit_code_ref`: the `test` commit is the RED, so no RED run is captured. G6 may still be
  `not_run`. v2–v5 logs still verify their G10.
- **v5** — G6 is one global entry again: the developer's declared mutation commands, judged
  together against one bar. G6 alone may be `not_run`, with a rationale, when no command is
  declared. v4 logs still verify with their two scoped entries.
- **v4** — G6 is recorded once per mutation scope with a `scope` field (`core`, `boundary`);
  its runner reads the break threshold from the checked-in config, so no `--break-at` flag is
  expected in `command_executed`. Evidence lives in one directory per story.
  `repo_root_rev` may be the parent of the evidence-only commit.

- **v3** — adds gate `G11` (line coverage meets the bar) and restates `G6` as an exit-code attestation rather than a score comparison: the runner's `--break-at` decides, so a log no longer records a number a reader must judge. Removes the `depthTier` reference, which no longer exists.
- **v2** — adds gate `G10` (RED observed) and the three per-cycle fields `red_stdout_ref`, `red_stdout_sha256`, `red_exit_code_ref`; everything a `v1` log declares is unchanged.

# Quality Gates — .NET Adapter

Concrete recipes that bind the gates of `quality-gates-evidence-contract` to the
.NET toolchain. Loaded ONLY when the producer detects a .NET stack.

## Detection

Activate this adapter when ANY of the following resolves at the repo root:
- `*.sln` or `*.slnx`
- `Directory.Packages.props`
- `**/*.csproj`

If multiple stacks coexist, run each adapter and concatenate gate entries.

## Output paths (relative to repo root)

```
.copilot-tracking/skraft-plans/{projectSlug}/evidence/{date}/{story}/
```

Throughout this file, `$EV` is shorthand for that directory — one per story, never shared,
ignored by Git (`.copilot-tracking/skraft-plans/*/evidence/` in `.gitignore`), never committed —
and `$LOG` for `$EV/qg-{story}.json`. `<skill>` is this skill's folder, the one holding this
SKILL.md: every script below ships in `<skill>/scripts/`, never in the consumer repository.

`$EV` holds the log and the screenshots, nothing else. `capture.mjs` runs a command without a
shell, prints the last 40 lines of its output and records the gate(s) it attests in `$LOG` —
`pass` on exit 0, `fail` otherwise, the last output line as `summary`; it exits with the
command's code, in bash and PowerShell alike. No `.stdout`, `.exit` or hash file is written,
and no agent ever types a status.

## Producer flow at the end of the story

One command runs every gate, records each verdict in `$LOG` and runs `qg-verify`; it exits with
`qg-verify`'s verdict and commits nothing:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/qg-collect.mjs" --root . --log "$LOG" [--screenshot {png} …]
```

It refuses a `$LOG` Git does not ignore. It prints one line per gate, then the verdict. A `fail`
or `inconclusive` is yours to fix: fix the code, then run it again. `qg-verify` takes the DELIVER
and DISTILL bases the pipeline recorded; pass `--base` / `--red-base` only outside a pipeline.

## test.acceptance / test.unit — Tests pass

One run of the full suite attests both gates. The full suite includes the
`*.ArchitectureTests` project (NetArchTest / ArchUnitNET) when the repository has one: a broken
architecture rule fails `test.unit`. `qg-collect` writes the TRX report to a throw-away folder
outside the repository and records its counters as `metrics`. By hand:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/capture.mjs" --log "$LOG" --gate test.acceptance,test.unit -- dotnet test --nologo
```

## build.compile / build.lint — Build and static analysis

Use the analyzers wired into the build (Roslyn analyzers, `TreatWarningsAsErrors=true`): one
build attests both gates.

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/capture.mjs" --log "$LOG" --gate build.compile,build.lint -- dotnet build --nologo --no-incremental
```

## test.no-mocks-core — No mocks in Domain/Application

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/no-mocks-in-core.mjs" --root . --log "$LOG"
```

The script scans every `*.Domain` and `*.Application` project at any depth, plus the
`*.Domain.*Tests`, `*.Application.*Tests` and `*.UnitTests` projects, for mocking
frameworks (Moq, NSubstitute, FakeItEasy, AutoMoq). It prints one hit per line and records the
gate: `pass` on exit 0, `fail` with the number of hits otherwise.

## commit.convention and test.integrity — derived by qg-verify

Nothing to record: `qg-verify` reads every commit since the DELIVER base and checks its full
message, and guards every test file DISTILL's `test` commit holds — a later commit may only add
lines to it, unless its message records `PLAN_DEVIATION:`. No commit list, no cycle, no snapshot.

## evidence.screenshots — Frontend stories

A story whose commits touch a `@visual` scenario, `tests/e2e/`, a `package.json` declaring
`react` or a `playwright.config.*` records at least one screenshot taken by
`playwright-evidence`. Pass each PNG with `--screenshot`; `qg-collect` copies it into
`$EV/screenshots/` and records its sha256 (by hand: `node "<skill>/scripts/gate-log.mjs" --log "$LOG" --screenshot {png}`).

## Not run by this adapter

Architecture (`arch.boundaries`), coverage (`ci.coverage`) and mutation (`ci.mutation`) are not
pipeline gates. Coverage at 100% of Domain and Application and the mutation step run in the
project's CI; the developer runs `/skraft-mutation` by hand. Never record them in the log.

If a tool is unavailable in the environment (no SDK), the
gate is recorded `fail` with its error as summary — NOT `not_applicable`. The
contract treats unverifiable gates strictly so the lens can collapse them to
`inconclusive` upstream.

(`node "<skill>/scripts/qg-verify/cli/qg-verify.mjs" --log <path>`, bundled in this skill;
`<skill>` is the folder holding this SKILL.md) derives everything else from Git — the commits
since the DELIVER base and every RED acceptance test — and judges the verdict. Nobody re-runs a
gate; the project's CI runs them again on the pull request.

## Where the artifacts live — never in Git

One directory per story, never shared with another story, **ignored by Git**. It holds the log
and, for a frontend story, its screenshots — nothing else:

```
.copilot-tracking/skraft-plans/{projectSlug}/evidence/{date}/{story}/
├── qg-{story}.json      # the evidence log (this contract): verdicts only
└── screenshots/         # evidence.screenshots, frontend stories
```

The consumer project's `.gitignore` holds this line:

```gitignore
.copilot-tracking/skraft-plans/*/evidence/
```

Nothing under `evidence/` is ever committed: not the log, not a screenshot. No tool output,
exit-code or hash file is written either. `qg-verify` fails a v7 log whose evidence directory
holds a file Git tracks.

A screenshot `ref` is relative to the project's tracking directory
(`evidence/{date}/{story}/screenshots/home.png`). Tool run folders (Stryker HTML, TRX, logs)
never land here.

The test plan (`details/{date}/test-plan-{story}.md`, written by DISTILL) stays where it is: with
the screenshots, it is what the QA reads.

## Schema (`qg-{story}.json`)

The stack adapter's scripts write it — `capture.mjs` and the no-mocks scan for each gate,
`gate-log.mjs` for screenshots and `not_applicable` gates, or `qg-collect.mjs` for all of them on
.NET. Each write stamps `repo_root_rev` with `HEAD` and `produced_at` with the time.

```json
{
  "$schema": "quality-gates-evidence/v7",
  "story": "string — story identifier, from the file name qg-{story}.json",
  "produced_at": "ISO-8601 UTC timestamp",
  "producer": "software-engineer",
  "tech_adapter": "string — the quality-gates-<tech> skill whose scripts wrote it",
  "repo_root_rev": "string — git rev-parse HEAD (the last work commit)",
  "gates": [
    {
      "id": "test.acceptance",
      "label": "Acceptance test(s) pass",
      "status": "pass | fail | not_applicable",
      "command_executed": "the command the script ran",
      "summary": "last line of its output, e.g. Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: 15",
      "metrics": { "tests_total": 15, "tests_passed": 15, "tests_failed": 0 }
    },
    {
      "id": "evidence.screenshots",
      "label": "Frontend screenshots captured",
      "status": "pass",
      "screenshots": [
        { "ref": "evidence/{date}/{story}/screenshots/home-rejected.png", "sha256": "hex sha256 of the PNG bytes" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`metrics` is optional (the .NET adapter reads it from the TRX report). A `not_applicable` gate
carries a `rationale` instead of a command.

## Gates (fixed identifiers, `type.description`)

The `id` field uses a fixed taxonomy. Tech adapters MAP their tools to these ids;
they do NOT invent new ones. Adding a gate id is a contract change (new schema version).

| id | label | what it attests | before v7 |
|----|-------|-----------------|-----------|
| `test.acceptance` | Acceptance test(s) pass | the BDD/acceptance scenario for the active story is green | G1 |
| `test.unit` | All unit tests pass | the full unit suite is green; on .NET it includes the architecture tests | G2 |
| `build.compile` | Build passes | compilation / static type-check succeeded | G3 |
| `build.lint` | Static analysis pass | linter / analyzer reported no blocking issue; carries the boundary rules of the stack (ESLint `boundaries/*`, Python `import-linter`) | G4 |
| `test.no-mocks-core` | No mocks in Domain/Application core | the adapter's scan of the Domain/Application projects and their unit tests found nothing | G7 |
| `evidence.screenshots` | Frontend screenshots captured | the story's frontend outcome is shown by at least one hashed screenshot; required for a frontend story | — |
| `commit.convention` | Conventional commit policy | *derived by `qg-verify`, never in the log*: every commit since the DELIVER base satisfies the shared policy below | G8 |
| `test.integrity` | No test tampering (RED→GREEN integrity) | *derived by `qg-verify`, never in the log*: every test file a `test` commit holds only grows afterwards | G9 |

Architecture, coverage and mutation are not pipeline gates. The project's CI runs them
(coverage with a minimal bar and no exclusion, mutation as its own step); the developer runs
`/skraft-mutation` by hand. A v7 log never carries `arch.boundaries`, `ci.coverage`,
`ci.mutation` nor any `G<N>` id: `qg-verify` reports an unknown id as `inconclusive`, and a
derived id (`commit.convention`, `test.integrity`) recorded in the log as `inconclusive` too.

The RED is DISTILL's `test` commit: every acceptance test, committed before DELIVER starts and
before the code that makes it pass. No RED run is captured, no snapshot is written, and the
producer lists no commit and no cycle: `qg-verify` reads them from Git.

A gate that is genuinely irrelevant for the story uses `status: "not_applicable"` and
MUST include a `rationale` field explaining why. `not_applicable` is **never** a substitute
for `fail` or for missing evidence.

## Frontend stories — screenshots are mandatory

A story is frontend when a commit since the DELIVER base touches at least one of:

- a `.feature` file holding a `@visual` scenario;
- a path under `tests/e2e/`;
- a `package.json` declaring `react` (dependencies, devDependencies or peerDependencies);
- a `playwright.config.*` file.

A frontend story records `evidence.screenshots` with `status: "pass"` and at least one
screenshot — `node "<adapter>/scripts/gate-log.mjs" --log "$EV/qg-{story}.json" --screenshot <png>`
copies each PNG into `evidence/{date}/{story}/screenshots/` and records its `ref` and the sha256
of its bytes. Any other story omits the gate or records it `not_applicable` with a rationale.

## Falsification surface (what qg-verify checks)

`qg-verify` takes the DELIVER base (`--base`, default: the one the pipeline recorded) and the
DISTILL base (`--red-base`, default: idem). The quality-gates lens reports its verdict and checks
only the commit policy it cannot (approved feature scope, `Refs`/`Closes` issue line).

| What | How it is falsified |
|------|---------------------|
| `repo_root_rev` | resolves, and is `HEAD` |
| evidence directory | no file under it is tracked by Git |
| `gates[].status` | written by a script from an exit code; `fail` fails the log |
| `gates[].metrics.tests_failed` | for `status: "pass"` MUST be `0` |
| `gates[].screenshots[]` | each file MUST exist; the sha256 of its bytes MUST equal the declared value |
| `commit.convention` | every commit of `base..repo_root_rev`, read from Git |
| `test.integrity` | the test files of the `test` commits since the DISTILL base are guarded: each later commit that touches one may only ADD lines (`git show` of its parent against `git show` of the commit), unless its message records `PLAN_DEVIATION:` |
| frontend detection | computed from the files of `base..repo_root_rev` at `repo_root_rev` |

A test file is a `.feature`, a file under a `test`, `tests`, `__tests__`, `spec`, `specs` or `e2e`
folder, or a file named as a test (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, `*Tests.cs`, `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`).
The production stubs DISTILL commits with the RED are not guarded: the GREEN rewrites them.

## commit.convention — Full-message verification

Each commit's actual Git message: `type(feature): subject`, with the
approved feature scope and `Signed-off-by` trailer from `git commit -s`. For a
known issue, the final body line is `Refs: #N` for intermediate work or
`Closes #N` only when the whole issue is genuinely finished and all required
gates pass. Omit the issue line when unknown.

`qg-verify` checks the syntax and the sign-off; the lens checks the feature scope and the issue
line from the full messages. A verified violation is `fail`; a message nobody can read is
`inconclusive`.

## Producer rules (software-engineer side)

- Record the gates **once**, at the end of the story, after every work commit landed; each
  script stamps `repo_root_rev` with that last work commit, `HEAD`. Nothing is committed after it.
- The scripts refuse a log path Git does not ignore; append
  `.copilot-tracking/skraft-plans/*/evidence/` to the project's `.gitignore` in a work commit.
- Never write or edit the JSON by hand: every status comes from a script.
- Run `qg-verify` on the log before handing over; a `fail` or `inconclusive` is yours to fix.
- A failing gate is recorded `fail` and the log is still written. Do NOT delete the log to hide a
  failure — a missing log is `inconclusive` (NEEDS_REWORK), so hiding fails harder than disclosing.

## Verifier rules (qg-verify)

- `qg-verify` exits `0` pass, `1` fail, `2` inconclusive; the producer runs it on its own log
  before handing over, the reviewer runs it again, the lens reports its result.
- Any of the following → `verdict: inconclusive` (never `pass`):
  - the JSON is missing, or a required field is absent or malformed
  - a gate id is not a v7 gate (`GATE_UNKNOWN`), or a derived gate is recorded (`GATE_DERIVED`)
  - a screenshot does not exist, or its `sha256` does not match its bytes
  - `repo_root_rev` is not `HEAD` (the log describes an older tree)
  - no DELIVER base (`BASE_UNKNOWN`) or no DISTILL base (`RED_BASE_UNKNOWN`) is known
  - no `test` commit since the DISTILL base holds a test, while `test.acceptance` applies
  - a commit cannot be read
- Any of the following → `verdict: fail`:
  - a gate has `status: "fail"`
  - `metrics.tests_failed > 0` while `status: "pass"` (internal contradiction)
  - a commit since the DELIVER base violates the shared `commit.convention` policy
  - a guarded test file lost or changed a line without a `PLAN_DEVIATION:` in the commit
    (a `PLAN_DEVIATION` is reported as a `notice` for the lens to judge)
  - a file of the evidence directory is tracked by Git (`EVIDENCE_COMMITTED`)
  - a frontend story records no screenshot (`SCREENSHOTS_MISSING`)

## Schema versioning

`$schema: "quality-gates-evidence/v7"` is part of the contract. Bump the version
when adding/removing gates or fields; old logs MUST still be parseable with their
declared version.

- **v7** — gate ids become `type.description` (`test.acceptance`, `test.unit`, `build.compile`,
  `build.lint`, `test.no-mocks-core`; `commit.convention` and `test.integrity` derived from Git).
  Removes `G5` (architecture: covered by `test.unit` on .NET and `build.lint` on TypeScript and
  Python), `G6` (mutation: the project's CI, `/skraft-mutation` by hand) and `G11` (coverage: the
  project's CI). The log holds verdicts only: no `stdout_ref`, `stdout_sha256`, `stdout_tail`,
  `exit_code_ref`, `commits_covered` nor `test_integrity` — scripts write each status, and
  `qg-verify` reads the commits and the RED tests from Git. Adds `evidence.screenshots`, required
  for a frontend story. The log and the screenshots live in a Git-ignored directory;
  `repo_root_rev` is `HEAD`. v1–v6 logs still verify with their `G<N>` ids, captures, snapshots
  and evidence-only commit.
- **v6** — removes gate `G10` and the per-cycle fields `red_stdout_ref`, `red_stdout_sha256`,
  `red_exit_code_ref`: the `test` commit is the RED, so no RED run is captured. G6 may still be
  `not_run`. v2–v5 logs still verify their G10.
- **v5** — G6 is one global entry again: the developer's declared mutation commands, judged
  together against one bar. G6 alone may be `not_run`, with a rationale, when no command is
  declared. v4 logs still verify with their two scoped entries.
- **v4** — G6 is recorded once per mutation scope with a `scope` field (`core`, `boundary`);
  its runner reads the break threshold from the checked-in config, so no `--break-at` flag is
  expected in `command_executed`. Evidence lives in one directory per story.
  `repo_root_rev` may be the parent of the evidence-only commit.

- **v3** — adds gate `G11` (line coverage meets the bar) and restates `G6` as an exit-code attestation rather than a score comparison: the runner's `--break-at` decides, so a log no longer records a number a reader must judge. Removes the `depthTier` reference, which no longer exists.
- **v2** — adds gate `G10` (RED observed) and the three per-cycle fields `red_stdout_ref`, `red_stdout_sha256`, `red_exit_code_ref`; everything a `v1` log declares is unchanged.
